title: By the sky with its great stars.
subtitle: An oath to open a surah of comfort
then: This surah came when {trap}persecution in Makkah was at its height{/trap}. Ibn Abbas and others said the Buruj are the stars; Ibn Jarir said the twelve positions the sun and moon travel through. {idea}An ordered sky opens a surah meant to console.{/idea}
now: Your life feels out of control: the diagnosis, the layoff, the family fight. {reward}Step outside at night.{/reward} The stars are still on their exact paths, held by the One who holds you.
old: When my life falls apart, it feels like nobody is in charge.
new: The Lord who keeps the stars in order is in charge of my hardship too.
try: Look at the night sky tonight for one minute and hand one worry to Allah.

title: And by the Promised Day.
subtitle: A day on the calendar that will come
then: The hadith from Abu Hurayrah cited by Ibn Kathir says the Promised Day is {idea}the Day of Judgement{/idea}. To believers being persecuted in Makkah, this was a promise that their suffering had a court date.
now: You were cheated by someone who will never be caught. Your complaint went nowhere. {reward}The verse says there is a Day already promised for exactly this.{/reward}
old: Some wrongs will just never be put right.
new: Every unsettled wrong has a promised Day.
try: Leave one wrong done to you with Allah today, and stop replaying it.

title: And by the witness and what is witnessed.
subtitle: Days that see and days that are seen
then: A hadith cited by Ibn Kathir says the witness is {idea}Friday{/idea} and the witnessed is {idea}the day of Arafah{/idea}. It says Friday holds an hour in which a Muslim who asks Allah for good is given it. Others said the witnessed is the Day of Judgement.
now: Friday arrives as another busy workday, lunch rushed, phone buzzing. {reward}There is an hour in it where your dua is answered.{/reward}
old: Friday is just another day with a prayer in the middle.
new: Friday is a witness day with an hour of answered prayer hidden in it.
try: This Friday, set aside five minutes in the late afternoon just for dua.

title: Cursed were the people of the ditch.
subtitle: The story the oaths were leading to
then: Ibn Kathir relates the hadith of the boy and the king from Muslim: a boy's faith led a whole crowd to say {reward}we believe in the Lord of the boy{/reward}. The king had ditches dug and fires lit for anyone who would not give up faith.
now: You may never face fire, but you will face pressure: the joke at work about your prayer, the friend who says faith is old-fashioned. {idea}The story asks what you will hold on to.{/idea}
old: The ones with the power always come out on top.
new: Those who torment believers are the ones who truly lose.
try: Stand firm on one small part of your faith today when it would be easier to drop it.

title: A fire kept fed with fuel.
subtitle: Cruelty that was planned and maintained
then: Ibn Kathir says they dug a ditch, {trap}lit a fire in it and prepared fuel to keep it ablaze{/trap}, then asked the believers again to give up their faith. The believers still refused.
now: A grudge kept burning for years, fed with screenshots, old stories, and new complaints. {idea}Cruelty rarely stays alive on its own. Someone keeps feeding it.{/idea}
old: Harm that lasts just sort of happens.
new: Lasting harm is kept going by someone choosing to feed it.
try: Stop adding fuel to one conflict today: do not repeat the story.

title: They sat around it.
subtitle: Comfortable beside someone else's suffering
then: The verse pictures the persecutors seated at the edge of the ditch. {trap}They were not rushed or ashamed. They sat.{/trap} The surah introduction ties this to the Makkan chiefs who were also pressuring believers.
now: Someone is being humiliated in the group chat and you just watch, reading every message. {idea}Sitting comfortably beside harm is not neutral.{/idea}
old: If I am only watching, I am not part of it.
new: Sitting at ease while someone is hurt is a stance, not nothing.
try: Next time you see someone mocked today, say one kind word for them or leave.

title: They watched what they were doing to the believers.
subtitle: Witnesses to their own crime
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}were witnesses to what was done to these believers{/trap}. They could not claim later they did not know. And the surah adds that Allah too is Witness over everything.
now: You saw the colleague being pushed out unfairly. You saw the sibling left out of the inheritance talk. {idea}Seeing it makes you part of the record.{/idea}
old: I did not do it. I only saw it.
new: What I see clearly, I will be asked about.
try: Think of one unfairness you have watched quietly. Take one small step to help.

title: Their only crime was believing in the Mighty, the Praised.
subtitle: When faith itself is the accusation
then: Ibn Kathir says these believers committed no sin in their persecutors' eyes {trap}except their faith in Allah{/trap}. He adds that Allah is Mighty and Praiseworthy in all He decrees, {idea}even when the reason is unknown to many people{/idea}.
now: You are passed over for the team trip because you do not drink, or teased for fasting at school. {reward}If faith is the only thing they hold against you, you are in good company.{/reward}
old: If people hold my faith against me, I should hide it.
new: Being disliked only for believing is something to be proud of, not hide.
try: Thank Allah today for one way your faith makes you stand out.

title: His is the kingdom of heaven and earth, and He sees everything.
subtitle: The real owner of the ground they ruled

row.title: the king
sub: owned a ditch and an army

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah owns the heavens, the earth, and all between them, and {idea}nothing is concealed from Him{/idea}. The king seemed to own everything. The verse names the real Owner.
now: The manager who decides your contract, the landlord with your deposit. {trap}They seem to hold everything.{/trap} {reward}The verse reminds you who actually owns it all, and that He saw what they did.{/reward}
old: The person with power over me has the final say.
new: Allah owns everything, and sees how power is used over me.
try: Before a meeting with someone who has power over you, say: Allah is the real Owner.

title: Those who torment believers, then never repent, face the Fire.
subtitle: Even here, the door of repentance is named
then: Ibn Abbas and others said tormented here means they burned them. Yet Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: {reward}look at this generosity. They killed Allah's friends, and He still invites them to repent.{/reward}
now: You have hurt someone badly, maybe someone who was only trying to do right. {reward}If even the people of the ditch were offered repentance, the door is open for you.{/reward} Walk through it today.
old: What I did is too serious to be forgiven.
new: Allah invites even the worst wrongdoers back. The condition is only that I return.
try: Apologise to one person you have wronged, or ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.

title: Believers who do good get gardens with rivers. The great win.
subtitle: What the believers in the ditch truly gained
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {reward}the opposite of what is prepared for His enemies{/reward}. The introduction says the surah was meant to console believers in Makkah: stay firm, and you will be richly rewarded.
now: You lost the promotion because you would not bend the numbers. Friends drifted away when you changed. {reward}The verse calls what you kept the great win.{/reward}
old: Holding on to my faith keeps costing me.
new: What I keep by staying firm is the biggest success there is.
try: Write down one thing your faith has cost you, and next to it: the great win.

title: Your Lord's grip is truly severe.
subtitle: The oppressor's power is not the last word

row.title: the strong do as they like

then: Ibn Kathir says His punishment upon those who reject His Messengers and oppose His command is {idea}severe, great and strong{/idea}. Whatever He wants happens, in the blink of an eye or faster.
now: A bully at work or at home seems untouchable. {reward}This verse is for the one being pushed down.{/reward} {idea}And it is a check on you, the day you hold power over someone weaker.{/idea}
old: People with power will always get away with it.
new: Allah's grip is stronger than anyone's, so I fear misusing my own small power.
try: Think of someone with less power than you. Treat them with extra gentleness today.

title: He begins creation, and He brings it back.
subtitle: Death does not escape Him
then: Ibn Kathir says from His perfect power He begins creation and {idea}repeats it just as He began it, without opposition{/idea}. The believers burned in the ditch and the ones who burned them will both be brought back.
now: You watch a newborn's first breath in the delivery room and an old relative's last one in a hospice. {idea}The One who did the first can do it again.{/idea}
old: Bringing the dead back to life is hard to imagine.
new: Starting life was the harder thing, and He already did it.
try: Next time you see a baby or a seedling today, remember He will bring you back too.

title: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.
subtitle: Right after the severe grip, love
then: Ibn Kathir says He forgives the sin of whoever repents and humbles himself, {reward}no matter what the sin may be{/reward}. Ibn Abbas said Al-Wadud means {reward}the Loving{/reward}.
now: You fear Allah and think of Him as only a judge watching for mistakes. {reward}He names Himself the Loving, right next to the warning.{/reward}
old: Allah is mostly strict and waiting to punish me.
new: The same Lord with a severe grip is forgiving and loving to whoever turns to Him.
try: Call on Allah today as Ya Wadud, the Loving, in one dua.

title: Owner of the Throne, the Glorious.
subtitle: Above all creation
then: Ibn Kathir says He owns {idea}the Mighty Throne that is above all of creation{/idea}. The word glorious was recited two ways, describing either the Lord or the Throne, and both meanings are correct.
now: The boardroom on the top floor, the corner office, the throne of a king. {idea}Every seat of power is below His Throne.{/idea}
old: The people at the top have the final word.
new: Above every throne and every top floor is the Throne of the Glorious.
try: Say subhana rabbiyal a'la with full attention in your next sujud.

title: He does whatever He intends.
subtitle: No one can block His will
then: Ibn Kathir relates that Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, in his final illness, was asked whether a doctor had seen him. {reward}He said yes, the doctor said: I am the Doer of whatever I intend.{/reward} He meant Allah.
now: Waiting outside the scan room, refreshing the job portal, checking the visa status again. {reward}What He intends will happen. That is where the heart can rest.{/reward}
old: Everything depends on me making it work.
new: I do my part, and Allah does what He intends.
try: Do your best on one worry today, then say: Allah does what He intends, and let it go.

title: Has the story of the armies reached you?
subtitle: History as proof of the severe grip

row.title: no one could ward it off

then: Ibn Kathir says it asks whether news has reached you of {trap}the torment Allah sent on them, which no one could ward off{/trap}. It confirms verse 12 about the severity of His grip.
now: You feel safe because of your savings, your connections, your health. {idea}The verse asks you to look at who felt safe before you.{/idea}
old: The more backup I have, the safer I am.
new: No army or backup protects anyone from Allah's seizing.
try: Name the one thing you feel most secure because of. Thank Allah for it as His gift, not your shield.

title: Of Pharaoh and of Thamud.
subtitle: Two famous powers that fell
then: The introduction says: if the Makkans were proud of their hosts, {trap}the hosts of Pharaoh and Thamud were stronger and more numerous{/trap}. They should learn from the fate those met.
now: The company that seemed too big to fail. The person who seemed unbeatable at school. {idea}Point the lesson at your own pride, not at anyone else.{/idea}
old: I am strong enough that it will not happen to me.
new: Stronger people than me fell, so I stay humble.
try: Catch one moment of pride today and replace it with alhamdulillah.

title: Yet the disbelievers stay stuck in denial.
subtitle: Stories heard, nothing learned
then: Ibn Kathir says they are {trap}in doubt, suspicion, disbelief and rebellion{/trap}. They had heard the history and the warnings, and it changed nothing.
now: You know all the prophets' stories from childhood, could tell them by heart. {idea}The question is what any of them changed in how you live this week.{/idea}
old: Knowing the stories of the Quran is enough.
new: A story only helps me if it changes what I do.
try: Pick one Quran story you know well and draw one lesson to act on today.

title: And Allah surrounds them from behind.
subtitle: There is no exit from His reach
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}He has power over them and is able to compel them. They cannot escape Him or evade Him.{/idea} The introduction says His power has encircled them.
now: You change cities, change your number, start fresh, and the guilt still comes along. {reward}You cannot run from Allah, but you can run to Him.{/reward}
old: If I keep busy, I can avoid facing Allah.
new: He already surrounds me, so the only way out is toward Him.
try: Stop running from one thing today. Bring it to Allah in a quiet dua.

title: No, this is a glorious Quran.
subtitle: Not what the deniers called it
then: Ibn Kathir says glorious means {reward}magnificent and noble{/reward}. The surah ends by defending the very book the Makkans were rejecting.
now: The mushaf sits on a high shelf, dusted before guests arrive. Your phone has a Quran app you open in Ramadan. {idea}Glorious things deserve daily attention.{/idea}
old: The Quran is something I respect but rarely open.
new: This glorious book is meant to be read, not only respected.
try: Read one page of the Quran today, even slowly.

title: Inscribed in a Preserved Tablet.
subtitle: Guarded from any change
then: Ibn Kathir says it is {reward}among the most high gathering, guarded from any increase, decrease, distortion, or change{/reward}. The king in the story is gone. The words that describe him remain.
now: Apps update, news changes by the hour, the advice you read online last year is already rewritten. {reward}One text in your life is guarded from all of that.{/reward}
old: Everything changes, so nothing can be fully relied on.
new: The Quran is preserved, so I can build my life on it.
try: Memorise or review one short verse today and keep it with you.
